steps.text: Combine peas, water, and salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then stir in butter.
Whisk together cream, flour, and sugar in a small bowl. Stir mixture into peas. Cook over medium-high heat until thick and bubbly, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cream Peas
raw_recipe.description: These creamed peas are made with basic pantry staples, cook in just 10 minutes, and make a quick and easy side dish that goes well with everything.
raw_recipe.name: Cream Peas

recipeInstructions.text: Combine peas, water, and salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then stir in butter.
Whisk together cream, flour, and sugar in a small bowl. Stir mixture into peas. Cook over medium-high heat until thick and bubbly, about 5 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I thought these turned out delicious. However, due to previous reviews, I decided to add only 1/2 tsp of sugar to the mix, then added a few dashes of cumin and pepper. I agree that 2 Tb would be a bit much for the recipe. The cumin and pepper, and lowered sugar made this recipe a five star!

A tad too sweet and lacking in flavor, so back to the drawing board I went. Halved the sugar, added minced onion and garlic and subbed chicken broth for the water. The changes were minimal, but the finished product was much more appetizing. Thank you Stephndon for the recipe.

My Father loves creamed peas & pearl onions. It used to be in the frozen vegetable section at the grocery store. Can't find it anymore. I omitted the sugar (peas sweet enough), sauteed frozen peas & pearl onions in bacon grease before adding remaining ingredients. It was the perfect!

I used fresh peas, and 1% milk cause that's what I had on hand. I boiled the peas for 5 min. in 2/3c. milk, then stirred in the butter and the other ingredients, substituting the 1% milk for the cream. I reduced sugar to 1 tsp. and added a hint of nutmeg. It thickened right away and was delicious. No need to use the higher fat cream called for in the recipe, unless you want it really rich in calories and fat:)

order of operation is all wrong, make a roux first, I like to cook some bacon up first, and use the bacon fat as the bases of the roux. Add the flour and milk. stirring constantly. I prefer canned peas as frozen for this receipt are too firm. Add peas and cut up bacon. Serve over toast.
This is a great recipe. I made slivered sweet onions, sautéed in about 1 teaspoon butter, then set them aside.

I agree they were a tad too sweet for our taste but they were good nonetheless. I will give this recipe a thumbs up every time, if you want a more traditional gravy flavor make homemade white gravy Add peasto it with salt and pepper and onion of choice and it would be great
The possibilities are endless to make these as great as you would like them to be, so don’t be afraid to go out there and try your own gravy or mix it up and put your own flair to it enjoy

This was a good base recipe that was easy to modify. I cut the sugar in half, as recommended by other reviewers. I also added some chopped onion, pepper and cumin. With the modifications, it was perfect.

Brings me back to my childhood and I loved it.I would have given 5 stars but I slightly modified it.Omit the sugar and use canned sweet peas(they are sweet enough)or fresh steamed from the garden.Using cream is fine but for health use 2% milk.If you like add a pinch of nutmeg and watch guests try and figure what gives it that extra comforting feel while eating it with the maon dish.Thank you for reminding me of this childhood comfort food.

I substitued white sugar with 1 1/2 packets of Truvia. Still too sweet so next time I'll only do about 1/2 packet. I think 2 Tbl of flour made it a little too thick so next time I'll add 1 Tbl. It was lacking a little in flavor so I simply added pepper. But all in all, really great, easy and quick recipe.

This is works really well for the frozen peas. If you like it sweet, leave the sugar and add a few pinches of nutmeg. If something less sweet is what you are after, use less sugar (or none) and add some pearl onions and a little bit of garlic!! Great both ways.

My paternal grandmother used to make this dish often as a side to a meat and other v see vegetables, My mother didn't, are it because my dad dint care for the peas! However, at 75, I still make it, because I loved it as a child. I follow my grandmother's example by adding a few chopped onions and then a few bacon crumples to the too as a garnish. Thanks for adding this recipe to remind younger cook of an additional to prepare vegetables.
Perfect
We liked it. Looked at others comments and added onion, just 1tsp sugar and a bit more yummy butter

I grew up making this simple recipe and haven't made it for years. I used it as a side dish tonight with Sunday Fried Chicken, buttered potatoes, homemade sour dough bread. You would have thought my family had never eaten food before. My youngest ask if I would make it tomorrow night ... I promised I would make it again this week! I believe we have revived an old family favorite.
I absolutely love creamed peas and this recipe is so easy. I do add a little black pepper to them.
More like a country style recipe of the 1970’s. Very good, very easy and quick. I make these regularly, and even better when pored over toasted bread on a plate.
I use caned peas. I use the water in the peas. With four and sugar in 1 tbs. One splash of milk. Each makes a great sweet cream when added to boiling peas
delicious, omit the sugar and add a jar of dried beef to this and serve over boiled potatoes or fat slices of toast and you have S.O.S!!!!!
It was just like my Mom used to make. Yummy!
